subtopics.title: From Gross to Net — the Deductions

questions.question: A deduction is best described as:
options: The employee's own earned money, redirected on their behalf to an agreed destination
A cost the employer adds on top of gross
The employer's share of the pension

questions.question: PAYE deducted from employees is paid over to:
options: SARS — the employer collects the tax; it never owns it

questions.question: Which pair is calculated as a PERCENTAGE of gross (in our examples)?
The administrator: gross R8 800, deductions R1 100 + R660 + R88 + R450 + R60. Her net pay is:
options: R6 442 — gross less total deductions of R2 358

questions.question: A contribution differs from a deduction because it:
options: Is paid by the employer OVER AND ABOVE gross and never shrinks the employee's net
Appears only on the employee's payslip

questions.question: The Skills Development Levy (SDL) is unusual because:
options: It is deducted from the employee only
It has NO employee half — it is purely an employer levy of 1% of gross, paid to SARS
It is paid to the trade union
It is a fixed rand amount

questions.question: The employer's total contributions for the administrator (pension R660, UIF R88, medical R450, SDL R88) come to:
The TOTAL COST of employing her for the month is:
options: R10 086 — gross R8 800 plus employer contributions R1 286

subtopics.title: The Salaries Journal, the Wages Journal and the CPJ

questions.question: The column architecture of the SJ/WJ is:
options: Per employee: gross, a column per deduction, net pay — with the employer's contribution columns alongside

questions.question: The Salaries expense account is debited with:
options: The GROSS — the full expense of employing; only the net is credited to Bank

questions.question: Deductions withheld from employees become:
options: Creditors — amounts OWED to SARS, the pension fund, the UIF, the medical scheme and the union

questions.question: The payment to the pension fund through the CPJ carries:
options: Both halves — R660 plus R660 — debiting the creditor and crediting Bank

questions.question: Every payroll deduction is only legitimate if:
options: A written contract authorised it — hours, rate, multipliers and deductions by signature
The employer decides it is fair

questions.question: The payroll signature of nepotism is:
options: A name earning outside the scale — appointed above the advertised notch or promoted past waiting colleagues
Two workers on the same notch

questions.question: "Correct books, wrong conduct" describes:
options: A trial balance that does not level
Perfectly recorded pay that does not match responsibilities — arithmetic balancing while the practice is unjust
A journal with a missing column

questions.question: The employer's duties regarding union fees are:
options: To set the fee and keep it if unclaimed
To pay the fee on the employee's behalf as a contribution
To discourage membership to save costs
To deduct faithfully, pay over promptly, and respect the union's negotiating role

questions.question: The five stops the envelope makes are:
options: Tax, retirement jar, just-in-case insurance, doctor cover, the union
Bank, SARS, the owner, the shop, the till

questions.question: The crucial way to SEE the deductions is:
options: Nothing was taken FROM you — your own money was sent ahead to places you agreed it should go
The government takes whatever it wants
Net pay is a discount on gross

questions.question: Earned R8 800, received R6 442 — the R2 358 between them is:
options: The employer's profit on the worker
Redirected in the worker's name — deductions travelling to their agreed destinations

questions.question: "Save one, get one" describes:
options: The rand-for-rand pension match — the shop putting R660 beside the worker's R660

questions.question: The skills levy in the second envelope is:
options: 1% paid by the shop into the country's training pot — the worker's envelope never feels it

questions.question: The true monthly cost of the job is:
options: R10 086 — gross plus the second envelope of R1 286

questions.question: Mixing the two envelopes collapses the sum because:
options: Deductions shrink YOUR envelope; contributions are EXTRA on top and never touch your net

questions.question: The deal goes on paper before the first shift because:
options: Memory negotiates and paper doesn't — the contract is the worker's case if the envelope runs light
The law taxes written contracts less

questions.question: A shop that hires cousins over candidates "pays twice":
options: In double wages and double tax
Once in weaker work, once in every good worker who stops trying or leaves — the ladder stops motivating

questions.question: "Balancing is not the same as being right" means:
options: A payroll can record unfair pay in perfectly neat, balancing columns — the arithmetic cannot certify the justice

questions.question: One worker asking is a request; every worker asking together is:
options: A negotiation — the union's collective voice at the table where multipliers and minimums are agreed
